lesson.scenario: A cache fleet changes membership while a virtual-node ring remaps only the affected hash intervals.

steps.title: Install many ownership points
steps.narration: Each physical cache contributes 128 independently hashed virtual tokens, spreading small ring intervals across both machines.
action: Sort 256 tokens for nodes A and B

steps.narration: The first token clockwise is A@0x6A40, so A is primary; continuing clockwise selects B@0x6B02 as the distinct replica.

production.scenario: Fastly edge image caching places object keys on a global cache fleet while minimizing movement during capacity changes.
components: global browsers requesting product imagery from many edge regions
service boundary that maps content keys onto the current edge membership view
control-plane service that uses consistent hashing to keep object ownership stable during membership churn
durable authority in etcd for cache node health, weights, and ring epochs
store and serve the image objects for the owners chosen by the placement function
control path that drains unhealthy nodes and publishes new ring epochs safely
observability path for key movement, node skew, and miss storms during rebalance
flows: An image request hits the edge placement boundary before any origin fetch or cache lookup.
The boundary asks the consistent hashing service for the current owner set for the object key.
The placement function uses the authoritative membership registry and current ring epoch.
The request is sent to the selected edge owners that should already hold or fetch the image.
The rebalance controller writes safe membership updates and drain markers into the authority.
A new epoch invalidates old placement views and updates the placement service.
Dashboards show how many keys moved, which edges skewed hot, and whether the rebalance stayed within budget.
